do_not_train.reason: retrieval/coverage/selection failures are code paths, not model behaviour; the domain leak needs an intent check before generation, not weight changes

composition_rationale: Stage 6 base shares weighted toward multi-provision, range and partial (not-found) answers in the grounded prompt format, with refusal and non-fabrication categories kept; each model-side failure category adds a bounded boost to the dataset categories that train it.

recommended_validation.task_validation_set: held-out validation split of the Stage 6 dataset, stratified by category (16 examples)
recommended_validation.checkpoint_metric: task_score = mean of [validator status valid, every requested provision addressed, no unsupported/fabricated content, refusal correctness]; eval_loss only breaks ties
recommended_validation.candidate_rule: a checkpoint is a candidate only if its task_score is at least the base model's on the same examples
recommended_validation.final_comparison: Stage 5 dataset, base vs trained, controlled evidence and full pipeline, raw and repaired kept separate

recommended_early_stopping.note: stopping on loss bounds the run; selection never uses loss alone

risks: Stage 12/13 lesson: lower validation loss did not improve the task and taught over-refusal; every candidate must beat the base on task_score
verbatim-style multi-provision targets could bias the model toward quoting; acceptable for a regulatory system, measured by answer length and repair frequency
CPU training reaches roughly 100 optimizer steps overnight; the effect may be small
the Stage 5 set is 50 questions concentrated on part 820 and part 101; improvements there may not generalise
proceed_reason: 11 of 46 generated answers fail for model-side reasons with the evidence architecture working
